top_choice_rationale: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) is a mature, general method with three decades of documented use in medicinal and process chemistry and total synthesis, with a clean two-person allocation and a citation worded around the general catalytic method that handles Kosugi's precedent. What was new chemically was C-N reductive elimination from Pd amido complexes and the ligand design that suppressed beta-hydride elimination, which is not a rerun of the 2010 C-C coupling prize. Car-Parrinello is a clean, mature second choice but does not make molecules; the lipid nanoparticle proposal is important but has contested attribution and sits close to formulation; no award is ranked last because several mature, defensible achievements are available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile (Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr are on the committee, but no conflict with any proposed laureate is evident)
